Managing the gamemode.ini file with privileges.

This application manages the GameMode configuration file. The [gpu] options are applied by the daemon only when the file resides at /etc/gamemode.ini (privileged path): when you enable GPU options, you will be asked for the administrator password via pkexec.

GameMode reads multiple files in this order: /usr/share/gamemode/gamemode.ini (provided by the package), /etc/gamemode.ini, ~/.config/gamemode.ini and $PWD/gamemode.ini. Values from later files override earlier ones. This GUI writes to /etc/gamemode.ini, the location intended for the administrator's configuration (and one of the two, together with /usr/share, where the [gpu] section takes effect).

To use renice and core parking you must belong to the 'gamemode' group.

How often (in seconds) GameMode's "reaper" thread checks for exited clients, configuration file changes and CPU/iGPU power balancing. Lower values react sooner but use a bit more CPU; higher values are lighter but less responsive. Default: 5.

CPU governor set when entering GameMode. "performance" keeps cores at maximum frequency (less stutter and latency); "powersave"/"schedutil" use less power. Requires privileges to write the governor (pkexec).
CPU governor set when leaving GameMode, instead of the one active before. If left empty, GameMode restores the previous governor. Setting it (e.g. "powersave") avoids being stuck on "performance".

Platform (ACPI/firmware) profile set when entering: "performance" favours speed, "low-power" favours efficiency, "balanced" is in between. Affects fans, thermal limits and power. Not all systems support it.
Platform profile restored when leaving GameMode. If left empty, the previous one is restored.

CPU governor applied when the integrated GPU is under heavy load (GameMode sets it like the CPU governor). "powersave" favours the GPU when it is the one working. Available values are read from the kernel.
Ratio between integrated-GPU power (W) and CPU power (W) above which the iGPU is considered "under load" (typically 0.3–0.5). -1 disables the whole iGPU check (always uses desiredgov).

Soft real-time scheduler policy (SCHED_ISO): "auto" with 4 or more cores, "on" always, "off" never. Can improve smoothness and latency in games, but only takes effect on kernels that support SCHED_ISO (absent in upstream kernels).

Nice value (0–20) applied, negated, to game processes: higher = more CPU priority. Improves the game's responsiveness but can slow down the rest of the system. 0 = no change. Requires the "gamemode" group.

I/O priority for game processes: from 0 (highest) to 7 (lowest), or "off" to disable it, "reset" for the default CPU-priority-based behaviour. Higher = fewer loading hitches, but penalises other processes.
If enabled, GameMode prevents the screen saver and screen lock from activating while it runs. Avoids interruptions during play; disable it if you prefer to keep screen saving.
If enabled, GameMode disables the CPU "split lock" mitigation while playing. Can reduce performance drops in some games, but lowers protection against certain attacks: enable it knowingly.

Main switch for [gpu] optimisations: enabling it accepts responsibility and lets GameMode apply overclocks and NVIDIA/AMD power states. Without it the other [gpu] options are ignored. It only takes effect with the file at /etc/gamemode.ini (privileged path).
DRM device number of the card to control (usually 0), i.e. the number N in /sys/class/drm/cardN/. Useful only with multiple GPUs, to choose which card to optimise.

NVIDIA PowerMizer mode: 0 = Adaptive (balanced), 1 = Prefer Maximum Performance (maximum speed, more power/heat), 2 = Auto. Leave "— (default)" to make no change. Requires the coolbits extension enabled in nvidia-xconfig.

Offset in MHz on the GPU core's maximum clock: positive = faster (overclock), negative = slower (undervolt). 0 restores the default values, -1 (or empty) makes no change. Requires coolbits; values that are too high can cause instability or crashes.

Offset in MHz on the GPU memory's maximum clock: positive = faster, negative = slower. 0 restores the default values, -1 (or empty) makes no change. Requires coolbits; excessive overclocks can cause graphical artefacts or crashes.

AMDGPU performance level (power_dpm_force_performance_level): "low" reduces power and noise, "high" pushes performance to the maximum, "auto" lets the driver decide, "manual" is not supported here. Leave "— (default)" to make no change. Requires a recent AMDGPU module.

Pin (lock) the game processes to a specific set of cores, preventing them from migrating across cores: improves the consistency of performance and cache. Select cores with the checkboxes; if you select none, GameMode automatically detects the best cores (P-core/E-core on Intel).

Take offline (park) the cores not used by the game: reduces power and heat while keeping the active cores at maximum frequency (useful on CPUs with few fast cores). Requires membership in the 'gamemode' group. On many-core CPUs it can reduce system responsiveness while playing.

Adds the 'notify-send "GameMode started"' entry when GameMode starts: shows a desktop notification as GameMode activates. Handy to see at a glance when optimisations are on; requires a notification daemon running.
Adds the 'notify-send "GameMode ended"' entry when GameMode ends: shows a desktop notification as GameMode deactivates.
Commands/scripts run (via /bin/sh) when GameMode starts: one line = one command. Use it to stop services, set variables or launch custom scripts. Entries run in order.
Commands/scripts run (via /bin/sh) when GameMode ends: one line = one command. Use it to restore whatever you changed on start.
Maximum time (in seconds) granted to the start/end scripts: those that do not finish within this time are interrupted. Prevents a stuck script from delaying GameMode activation or deactivation.
